title: Compose blog module
description: Declarative block-based blogging with the Compose Blog Engine — JSON documents, public /blog routes, and an admin compose editor.

blocks.text: The blog-compose core module adds a full blogging stack without a WYSIWYG editor. Articles are Compose documents: ordered arrays of typed blocks (headings, explanations with highlight/underline phrases, code, terminal commands, callouts, and more). The interpreter renders those blocks as Tailwind-styled React components on /blog and in the admin live preview.

blocks.title: Live demo on this docsite
blocks.text: Open the Blog section in the sidebar: Live articles (/blog), Playground (/blog/playground), and this module guide. Posts use static JSON in content/blog/posts.json — same Compose shape as client templates.

By default, /blog pages are full-width without a docs-style left sidebar. To add an article list and on-page H2 table of contents (like this docsite blog section), install with the +sidebar suffix. This sets SITE.features.blogSidebar to true.

blocks.title: Dev Agency template example
blocks.text: The dev-agency vertical ships without blog-compose. See Developers → Templates → Dev Agency Website for a full walkthrough: tempjs add-module blog-compose+sidebar after generation, prisma db push, and optional BlogSection on the homepage.

blocks.code:
tempjs add-module blog-compose+sidebar
pnpm new-template bakery --modules blog-compose+sidebar,seo

blocks.text: You can also enable later in constants/site.ts: SITE.features.blogSidebar = true (requires blog-compose files already installed).

blocks.title: Module id: blog-compose
blocks.text: Feature flag SITE.features.blogCompose. Engine id compose (Compose Blog Engine). Future engines (e.g. rich-text editor) would use a different engine field and interpreter.
Install blog-compose alone or with other modules, then push the Prisma schema:

blocks.code:
tempjs add-module blog-compose
pnpm prisma db push
pnpm dev

items: lib/blog/compose/* — engine types, block registry, interpreter, and block components
BlogPost Prisma model with contentJson storing the Compose document
/api/blog-posts — public list of published posts; full CRUD when admin session is present
/blog and /blog/[slug] — public index and article pages
BlogSection — homepage teaser grid (SITE.blog.homepageLimit recent posts)
Admin → Blog articles tab — block picker, property forms driven by COMPOSE_BLOCK_REGISTRY, live preview

blocks.text: Each post stores JSON matching ComposeDocument. Blocks are validated with isComposeDocument() before save.

rows: Page title, H2, or H3 with design variants (default, accent, serif, underline-bar)
Body text with highlight and underline phrase arrays (exact substring match)
Code block with language and optional line numbers
Image with alt text and optional caption

blocks.text: Customize labels in constants/site.ts after install — section eyebrow/title for BlogSection, /blog page title, empty states, and view-all link text.

Scaffold templates get BlogSection on app/page.tsx when blog-compose is installed via new-template or add-module. Shipped vertical templates (hotel, real-estate) may need a manual import if you add the module later.
Use ComposeBlogRenderer anywhere in your template to render a static Compose document from code or a fetched JSON file — the engine is not limited to database-backed posts.
